original_claim.expected: Proposed for human ruling: the Tibetan says that under the stated inherent-existence hypothesis things should become clear when error stops, rather than cease; reconsider the English ellipsis that appears to say they should have disappeared. This is explanatory proposed correction only.
original_claim.evidence: Exact source ACIP: GSAL DU 'GRO DGOS KYI, LDOG PAR MI 'GYUR RO. Exact wylie: gsal du 'gro dgos kyi, ldog par mi 'gyur ro. Original HGM gsal = clear, illuminate, light, appear; ldog = stop, lost, ending, put an end to, refuse, turned back, stops. Thus the two predicates are opposed, and although they should have appears to elliptically repeat disappearance instead of clarity. C05:232 and C04:127 provide complete saved lexical clarity context. C16:813 is identical in ACIP, Wylie and English to C05:236; id/course/seq differ, and this does not establish independent publication or ingestion lineage. Registry checked for this wording and issue; no existing match found and none of the registered apparatus/formatting classes describes it. Context C05:232–241 is retained. Confidence is probable: neither an authorized corrected translation nor the origin of this shared reading is established.
